attributes.body_ja:
「ずつ」（漢字（かんじ）では「宛（ずつ）」）は、「一回（いっかい）に決（き）まった数（かず）や量（りょう）」があることを表（あらわ）す接尾語（せつびご）です。「ずつ」を副助詞（ふくじょし）と説明（せつめい）する教科書（きょうかしょ）もありますが、品詞（ひんし）によって使（つか）い方（かた）が変（か）わることはありません。

「ずつ」は、数字（すうじ）や量（りょう）を示（しめ）す語（ご）のあとに付（つ）いて、それが一（ひと）つのまとまりであることを表（あらわ）します。

豆知識（まめちしき）

漢字（かんじ）の「宛（ずつ）」には、「割（わ）り当（あ）てる」という意味（いみ）があります。この漢字（かんじ）は、人（ひと）が住（す）む場所（ばしょ）を表（あらわ）すときにも使（つか）われ、その場合（ばあい）は「あて」と読（よ）みます（住所（じゅうしょ）がその人（ひと）への割（わ）り当（あ）てとみなされます）。「ずつ」と読（よ）む場合（ばあい）も、「複数（ふくすう）のものを、一つのグループに割（わ）り当（あ）てる」というイメージを持（も）つと良（よ）いでしょう。
attributes.body:
ずつ, or 宛（ずつ） in its kanji form, is a suffix in Japanese that is used to highlight things that occur/exist in specific amounts. It is often translated simply as 'each', 'per', or 'at a time'. Depending on the source, ずつ may also be considered to be an adverbial particle. However, this will not change the way that it is utilized.

ずつ is used directly after the number/amount of something that it is highlighting as being the 'at a time' grouping.

Fun Fact

The kanji, 宛（ずつ）, literally means 'allotment', and refers to distinct groupings. It is regularly used in reference to where people live (their address being considered their 'allotment'). In these cases though, it has the reading 宛（あて）. For ずつ, 'allotment' may also be used as an accurate translation in almost all situations.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar
[AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.body: Both express the idea of 'each', but with different nuance and usage. ～ずつ attaches to quantity expressions like numbers or 少し to mean 'each' or 'at a time', e.g. 一つずつください 'Give me one of each.' or ちょっとずつよくなってきた 'It's gotten better a little at a time.' 当たり also attaches to Number + Counter, but means 'per' or 'apiece', e.g. １個当たり５００円です 'They're 500 yen apiece.'

attributes.body: Both convey the meaning of 'each', but differ in structure. ～ずつ attaches to quantity expressions to mean 'each' or 'little by little', e.g. 一つずつください 'Give me one of each.' or ちょっとずつよくなってきた 'It's gotten better a little at a time.' それぞれ appears before a phrase or with の and emphasizes individuality, e.g. 人はそれぞれ個性がある 'People each have unique qualities.'

attributes.body: Both deal with repetition or intervals, but in different ways. ～ずつ means 'each' or 'at a time' and attaches to quantity expressions, e.g. 一つずつください 'Give me one of each.' おきに follows time or distance intervals to mean 'every (A)', e.g. ５分おきに電車が来る 'Trains come every five minutes.'
